prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick), export connection to Grid Interface Relay (external). Out of scope: public grid beyond connection, non-farm port ops. Personnel keep procedural, safety, engineering authority; defined handoffs keep dispatch, marine, work supervision, stores accountable; procedures name authority for access approval, alarm response, service restoration. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; executes authorized control, reports state, adjusts output within limits, blocks commands conflicting with protection; produces Pitch Deviation Notice), Pitch System (changes blade angle per commands and local protection), Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (conversion within limits/interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor (health measurements), Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (alias Larkspur; captures blade imagery; suspended when weather, visibility or equipment unsafe). Substation: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. Shore: SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale; presents turbine status/control availability to authorized shore staff), Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay; staffed supervisory control, coordination), Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown; uses reviewed condition info for prioritization), Fleet Dispatch Console (alias Sable Orchard). Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (alias Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (alias Blue Granite; collects position broadcasts, time-stamped traffic view; produces Position Quality Flag on failed integrity/low confidence). Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanners; Warehouse System (alias Mosslight); Spares Hub; Work Permit Portal. Cybersecurity Gateway (alias Quiet Harbor): approved protocols/accounts only, deny-by-default; individual RBAC admin, logged time-limited privileged sessions; segmentation; boundary loss restricts remote admin without bypassing local protection. Interfaces retested after config changes (permitted functions available, prohibited paths blocked). Metocean Buoy (alias Copper Finch): wind, waves, current, temp, pressure; timestamped buffered. Remote commands: Control Engineer reviews alarms first; role-authorized, recorded; local protection has priority; control availability checked before use and after config changes. Remote observation supplements, never replaces physical inspection. Actors: HSE Officer, Field Supervisor (weighs observations before recommending work), Duty Planner (produces Transfer Manifest Addendum for approved vessel changes), Marine Coordinator (uses traffic picture), Vessel Master (go/no-go), Weather Analyst, Blade Specialist (plans inspection passes), Storekeeper, Port

New part:
S149: Work Permit Portal is the controlled entry point for planning, reviewing, approving, and closing maintenance work.
S150: Work Permit Portal is referred to as Redoubt in this section.
S151: The authorization lifecycle begins when a work request is entered with its location, scope, planned duration, and responsible team.
S152: The requester identifies the equipment affected and describes the intended work in terms that can be checked against operating constraints.
S153: Duty Planner reviews the request for completeness and assigns it to the appropriate planning queue.
S154: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.
S155: Work Permit Portal maintains the request record and its revision history throughout review and execution.
S156: The review identifies hazards, required controls, access arrangements, and any operating coordination needed before work can proceed.
S157: HSE Officer reviews the proposed controls when the task presents a material personnel or environmental risk.
S158: Technical reviewers confirm that the work scope is compatible with equipment condition and the planned maintenance method.
S159: SCADA Gateway uses the deviation notice to flag work packages that may require technical review.
S160: Marine Coordinator checks that the planned access method and timing are practical for the work location.
S161: Vessel Master confirms that the vessel plan can support the approved personnel and equipment transfer.
S162: Work Permit Portal records review decisions and returns incomplete requests to the requester with the required corrections identified.
S163: Warehouse System produces a Backorder Exception Slip when a requested component cannot be supplied by the planned issue date.
S164: The Duty Planner resolves outstanding supply and scheduling issues before submitting the request for authorization.
S165: The designated authorizing role grants permission only after required reviews and controls are recorded in the portal.
S166: Approval is limited to the stated scope, work location, time window, and assigned personnel.
S167: Field Supervisor verifies that the approved conditions remain valid before the crew starts work.
S168: Any material change to scope, conditions, or timing requires reassessment and may suspend the current authorization.
S169: Work Permit Portal records the start, pause, resumption, and completion of authorized work against the permit record.
S170: The responsible team reports completion status and outstanding issues before the permit is closed.
S171: Juniper Vale shall provide current operational status to permit reviewers when requested as part of the authorization check.
S172: Closed records remain available for audit, incident review, and future planning.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
